atoms.obligation: Work through each stage of the procedure in the order given, treating every stage as a binding requirement.
atoms.lesson: This skill guides the pipeline owner through a backfill end to end. Work the sections in order; each one names an obligation you can be held to.

atoms.obligation: Decide the processing order from what consumers need, and state which order you chose before starting.
atoms.lesson: Backfill newest-first when consumers care about recency, oldest-first when they care about continuity — decide which and say so.

atoms.obligation: Make every unit of work idempotent and independently retryable so repeating it leaves the same result.
atoms.lesson: Every backfill task must be idempotent and independently retryable: write to a staging location, then swap partitions atomically.

atoms.obligation: Limit the rate of background work so it never competes with scheduled production work for shared resources.
atoms.lesson: Throttle so the backfill never competes with the live schedule.

atoms.obligation: Checkpoint progress as you go so an interrupted run resumes where it stopped instead of restarting.
atoms.lesson: Checkpoint progress so a killed run resumes rather than restarts.

atoms.obligation: Adopt one boundary convention for ranges everywhere and state it explicitly.
atoms.lesson: Adopt [start, end) everywhere and state it. The convention has to hold across the whole backfill, not per task.

atoms.obligation: Manually verify the boundary cases against the produced output before accepting the results.
atoms.lesson: Manually verify the edge partitions against produced output — off-by-one at the window edges is the modal failure.

atoms.obligation: Stop and escalate whenever you cannot satisfy a stated requirement, rather than proceeding without it.
atoms.lesson: If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate. This applies to the time-window arithmetic: adopting [start, end) everywhere and manually verifying the edge partitions against produced output.

atoms.obligation: Produce a record complete enough for an independent party to reproduce the run exactly.
atoms.lesson: Produce a manifest sufficient for an independent re-run: invocation command, image digest, locked dependency set, seeds, and run window.

atoms.obligation: Verify the reproduction record by executing it once in a clean environment before relying on it.
atoms.lesson: Prove it works by executing it once in a fresh environment; an unverified manifest is a guess.

atoms.obligation: Estimate the cost of a large run before launching it, covering every component of the total.
atoms.lesson:
Apply this before the backfill leaves your hands.

Estimate cost before launching anything large: scenes x cost-per-scene for compute, bytes x rate x months for storage, plus egress.
atoms.anchor: 4. Estimate compute and storage cost before running for this backfill

atoms.obligation: Compare the estimate against the approved budget and obtain sign-off once it passes the agreed threshold.
atoms.lesson: Compare against the budget line and get sign-off past the agreed threshold. A run that finishes and blows the quarter's budget is a failed run.
atoms.anchor: 4. Estimate compute and storage cost before running for this backfill

atoms.obligation: Write the completion criteria before starting the work, and never add criteria after the fact.
atoms.lesson: Completion criteria are written first. No post-hoc criteria, no unverifiable ones — a criterion you cannot check is not a criterion.
atoms.anchor: 5. Definition of done: what is required

atoms.obligation: Verify each completion criterion at the end, item by item, with evidence for each one.
atoms.lesson: Completion criteria are verified last, item by item, each with its evidence. No post-hoc criteria, no unverifiable ones.
atoms.anchor: 5. Definition of done: what is required

atoms.obligation: Annotate the units, spatial reference and time zone of every value you store or pass on.
atoms.lesson:
Apply this before the backfill leaves your hands.

Annotate units, CRS and time zone everywhere.
atoms.anchor: 6. Be explicit about units, CRS and time zones — non-negotiable

atoms.obligation: Store values in the agreed standard units and reference systems, leaving local formats to the presentation layer.
atoms.lesson: Storage is SI, EPSG:4326 for coordinates, equal-area for area maths, UTC for time. Local formats belong to the presentation layer alone.
atoms.anchor: 6. Be explicit about units, CRS and time zones — non-negotiable

atoms.obligation: Record the outcome of this step in the notes kept for the work.
atoms.lesson: Record the outcome of this step in the backfill notes — the annotation of units, CRS and time zone is not done until it is written down there.
atoms.anchor: 6. Be explicit about units, CRS and time zones — non-negotiable

atoms.obligation: Measure the current state before making any change, under the same conditions you will measure again later.
atoms.lesson:
This section applies to every backfill without exception.

Capture the current numbers first — latency, cost, accuracy, coverage, whichever the change targets — under the conditions you will re-measure in later. Without a baseline taken under matched conditions, any improvement you report is a story.
atoms.anchor: 7. Measure the current state before changing it — non-negotiable

atoms.obligation: Write down how to undo a change, how long the undo takes and what it loses, before making it.
atoms.lesson:
Apply this before the backfill leaves your hands.

Before any change reaches a shared environment, write down how to undo it, how long the undo takes, and what is lost if you use it.
atoms.anchor: 8. Have a rollback path before you change anything — non-negotiable

atoms.obligation: Test the recovery procedure first whenever the undo path depends on restoring from a backup.
atoms.lesson: If the undo is 'restore from backup', test the restore first.
atoms.anchor: 8. Have a rollback path before you change anything — non-negotiable

atoms.obligation: Give every irreversible step a named approver and a scheduled time instead of improvising it.
atoms.lesson: Irreversible steps get a named approver and are scheduled, never improvised.
atoms.anchor: 8. Have a rollback path before you change anything — non-negotiable

atoms.obligation: Stop and escalate whenever you cannot satisfy a stated requirement, rather than proceeding without it.
atoms.lesson: If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate. This applies to the rollback path: the written undo procedure, its duration and its losses, the tested restore, and the named approver for irreversible steps.
atoms.anchor: 8. Have a rollback path before you change anything — non-negotiable

atoms.obligation: Record for every output the inputs, versions, time window, code revision and configuration it came from.
atoms.lesson:
Apply this before the backfill leaves your hands.

Every artefact you produce must be traceable back to its inputs. Record, for each output: the source dataset identifiers and versions, the acquisition window, the processing code revision (git SHA), and the configuration hash.

atoms.obligation: Store the origin record alongside the output itself, not in a separate document that will drift.
atoms.lesson: Store this beside the output, not in a separate wiki page that will drift.

atoms.obligation: Treat any output that cannot state where it came from as unfit to publish.
atoms.lesson: If an output cannot state where it came from, treat it as unpublishable.

atoms.obligation: Confirm every required step is complete against the closing checklist before finishing the work.
atoms.lesson:
- [ ] Backfill sequencing and idempotency
- [ ] Get the time-window arithmetic right
- [ ] Emit a reproducibility manifest
- [ ] Estimate compute and storage cost before running
- [ ] Close against an explicit definition of done
- [ ] Be explicit about units, CRS and time zones
- [ ] Measure the current state before changing it
- [ ] Have a rollback path before you change anything
- [ ] Record provenance and lineage
